newsitem.title: THAILAND: Discounts seen given by hurt property developers.
newsitem.headline: Discounts seen given by hurt property developers.

text.p: Cash-strapped Thai property developers are expected to offer discounts to buyers to offset a continued slump in the sector as the government declines to offer any more subsidies, a research report said on Monday.

Thaimex Finance and Securities Plc said loans extended by two government-run banks at lower than market interest rates of between 9.0-12.75 percent showed that plenty of demand still existed for housing.
The two banks offered loans totalling 17.5 billion baht to housing borrowers last week.

Analysts had said earlier that any positive impact of the loans offered would be limited by an estimated absorption of only 12,000-20,000 housing units in a market believed to contain about 300,000 empty units.
The Thai property sector has been depressed by a glut and high interest rates which have discouraged loan taking.

"The problem is not lack of demand but rather high prices and interest rates. Moves to stimulate demand by offering buyers effective price reductions will meet with immediate success; those that make house purchase easier but not cheaper will have less impact," Thaimex said.

Some developers were now offering as much as 50 percent discount if buyers paid in cash while some held firm on prices in the hope that the government would launch similar loan programmes in future to encourage sales.

"We expect that discount plans will spread as developers' resistance to effective price reductions begins to weaken in the face of the continued slump and the government declines to offer any more outright subsidies," the report said.
